strings.name: Shuji Nakamura
strings.summary: After Tokushima University, Nakamura joined Nichia and developed gallium-nitride materials and high-brightness blue LEDs, advancing efficient white lighting. He later taught at UCSB and continued solid-state-light research. He shared the 2014 physics Nobel with Isamu Akasaki and Hiroshi Amano. His employee-invention compensation lawsuit against Nichia settled in 2005, prompting debate on inventors’ treatment.
